end.summary:
Distinguished observation and hypothesis using a dog, bell, and door example; this was shown on a new-situation question.
Practised that laws describe repeated patterns and theories explain them; next time, check the distinction in another example.
Practised the scientific meaning of theory versus its everyday meaning; the difference was not steady yet.
Practised how repeated evidence and conditions can affect scientific ideas; this still needs checking next time.
The mix-up that theories become laws was corrected later; the idea that a theory is only a guess was also corrected later.
end.parentNote: Asha practised sorting observations, hypotheses, laws, and theories with a dog-and-bell example, and Tara identified the observation and testable guess. They also worked on the key distinction that laws describe patterns while theories explain them. Tara first treated theories as guesses and as ideas that become laws, but later corrected both points; the evidence-and-conditions part still needs more practice. At home, ask Tara to label one everyday example as observation, hypothesis, law, or theory and say what evidence could change the idea.
